summary:
Deviations: none.
Method audit: 34 recall misses found (26 added, 2 folded into existing items, 6 low or out of scope); root causes and fixes are in the errors section.

Missed items: weekly audit found 34 the daily runs missed, led by DOJ's Nov 2 Supreme Court bid to hold 20,000 California ballots

ERRORS AND INCOMPLETE ITEMS
- Source failures (informational) | TVG Daily Brief for Nov 2: "failed at its site (client_error)" (Oct 26-30 issues loaded); Just Security Early Edition: client_error (its home page loads again, Nov 1, but stays on the blocked list); Reuters, AP, Politico: SITE_BLOCKED "Access to this website has been blocked"; The Hill article pages: client_error | Why not done: hard blocks; the audit used wire copies on local sites, aggregators and newsletters instead.
- Stale sources (week 1 of 3) | Anadolu world served an April 27, 2024 copy; White House presidential actions newest item Oct 28; Times of Israel and Ground News (already removed) still stale at Oct 27 | Why not done: the pages themselves are stale; a page moves to the blocked list after three straight weekly failures.
- Recall misses: court rulings and grand juries (Hutchinson no-bill, Essayli ruling, Los Angeles stop order, Rochon ads order, child-asylum order) | These are checks on the Justice Department and immigration enforcers that change what they can do | Should have been caught by the world collector's aggregator pages, but those show only the current day, so a ruling that broke on a busy day scrolled off. Proposed fix: add one daily search, "judge rules Trump administration" plus the date, to the world collector.
- Recall misses: DOJ's Supreme Court filing on California ballots (Nov 2), Pezeshkian's talks mandate (Nov 2), Boasberg list order (Oct 30) | Politico Playbook PM arrives in the afternoon, after the morning run | Proposed fix: the next morning's newsletter pass should read the previous day's Playbook PM and Axios PM (both are in the inbox).
- Recall misses: White House Cook hearing moved to December (Oct 30), Arizona noncitizen-registration probe (Oct 30), Cameroon aid-for-deportees deal (WSJ, Oct 29), Pentagon budget draft (Politico, Oct 30), House Democrats' Epstein report (Oct 26), IAEA missing uranium (Oct 27), Russian gas-transit pitch (WSJ, Nov 2), Rubio-Venezuela meeting (Nov 2), tanker attacks (Nov 1), Pentagon watchdog declining the Starlink probe (Oct 28), State's Jeremy Lewin leaving (Oct 27), DOJ election monitors (Oct 31) | Only reachable through wire copies or outlets the collectors do not read; the newsletter inbox has no editions before Oct 30 | Proposed fix: the same daily court-and-agency search above, plus one Bloomberg/WSJ-relay search per issue when a day has fewer than two independent sources.
- Recall misses from the TVG digest the collectors listed but triage dropped as off-topic: DFC investment ceiling to $205B and a Mozambique graphite stake, DOE's $5B Constellation nuclear loan, DHS ban on Acronis, Greece's Black Sea truce call | Proposed fix: keep any dated agency act from the digest as a weight-2 item instead of dropping it.
- Not added (low or out of scope): VA psychedelic therapy push, Air Force hypersonic missile production, Army interceptor award to Lockheed, CISA 2030 strategy, US-Japan missile co-production (headline only), Trump backing El Salvador's Haiti troop surge | Why not done: no effect on what the tracked factions want or can do.
- Model audit proposals not applied (single or search-level sources): Katie Zacharia reportedly left as press secretary about Oct 16; Kristi Noem's State adviser role is disputed; the Russia policy line should mention the $2.1B Patriot sale Ukraine and partners pay for | Why not done: needs a read article or a second week of evidence.
- Still headline only: Hegseth as a possible appointee to Marsha Blackburn's Senate seat if she becomes Tennessee governor | Tennessee Lookout and two other outlets failed with client_error.

CONSEQUENTIAL NEWS
- Justice Department asks the Supreme Court to hold 20,000 California ballots (Nov 2; Roll Call, Politico). DOJ says about 20,000 California registrants may be noncitizens and wants their mail ballots set aside until checked; a federal judge refused and the Ninth Circuit rejected DOJ twice (Oct 26 and Oct 30), and a Los Angeles County review found many names are not even on the rolls. The justices can act before or after the count. | Consequence: keeps the Maximalists' (the faction running DOJ, FBI and immigration enforcement) noncitizen-voting claim alive into certification; no ballot has changed status; documented filing, outcome open.
- Grand jury refuses to indict Cassidy Hutchinson (Oct 27; ABC, Washington Post). DOJ sought charges against the former Trump White House aide for lying to the Jan. 6 committee, part of a run of cases against Trump critics that includes new charges against James Comey (Oct 26). A Washington grand jury declined; DOJ can try again. | Consequence: hurts the Maximalists by raising the cost of critic prosecutions in Washington; documented.
- White House postpones its Lisa Cook hearing to December (Oct 30; Kevin Hassett on Bloomberg TV). Trump is trying to fire Fed Governor Cook over mortgage-fraud allegations she denies; courts kept her seat, so the White House created its own hearing, set for Nov 5. Her lawyer said she is unavailable until after the Dec 8-9 Fed meeting, and no new date is set. | Consequence: Cook votes at the December rate meeting, where she dissented for a hike in October; the removal effort is intact but slower; reported (official on record).
- Judge bars immigration stops based on appearance in Los Angeles and six counties (order Oct 23, public Oct 29; Newsweek, LA Times). Judge Maame Frimpong requires reasonable suspicion and cites a "mountain of evidence" of stops of people who look Latino; the administration appeals, and the Supreme Court stayed a similar order of hers in September 2025. | Consequence: limits the Maximalists' street-arrest tactics in Southern California, provisionally; documented.
- Judge rules Los Angeles prosecutor Bill Essayli is serving unlawfully (Oct 27; AP). Courts have rejected the administration's practice of keeping interim US attorneys past legal limits in New Jersey and Nevada; Judge Michael Seabright now applies that to Essayli, whose office has charged protesters in the immigration crackdown. The ruling is stayed and he keeps serving. | Consequence: exposes the Maximalists' Los Angeles cases to challenge if the stay ends; documented.
- Judge orders three taxpayer-funded administration ads taken down (Oct 30; AP). In a Common Cause suit over 13 government ads it called campaign messaging, Judge Jennifer Rochon ordered three ("$5,000 to Americans", "No Tax on Tips", "Cost of Socialism") removed and barred their spread through the MAGA Inc. super PAC. | Consequence: small loss for the Operation (the White House political team running the campaign) in the final week; documented.
- Arizona's US attorney opens a noncitizen-registration case against three voter groups (Oct 30; DOJ release, Democracy Docket). Timothy Courchaine referred the groups to the FBI and urged state and Maricopa County officials to review registrations; DOJ now has such probes in California, Alaska, Washington, North Carolina and Arizona. | Consequence: widens the Maximalists' election pressure into a battleground state; no charges; documented act, my reading on effect.
- State reportedly trades $35M in military aid to Cameroon for taking other countries' deportees (Oct 29; WSJ, single outlet). The aid would go to a Cameroonian unit accused of abuses; State has not confirmed. | Consequence: gives the Maximalists a new third-country removal outlet at a reputational cost to Rubio's State Department; reported, provisional.
